scope: Summary and Introduction author prose only. Formula verification and chart/table distillation remain paused.
source_generation: v10 fresh-native text, separate from historical and NFKC views
counting_policy: Eight editorial text groups are navigation aids, not eight visually certified paragraphs. No visual_paragraph_count, quantitative layout or full G4 acceptance is assigned.
interpretation_policy: Claims, support roles, consequences and next-links are root descriptions of observable prose. A stated purpose, assumption, rationale or forecast is not upgraded into an executed validation. Source qualifiers and editorial reuse boundaries are kept separate.

groups.dominant_move: Introduce an analytical deliverable through the decisions and forecast it is intended to support.

claim.content: The proposed index is intended to distinguish cases and identify priority sectors, supporting planning, allocation and a future outlook.

support.content: The prose explains the intended use sequence: identify urgent issues, formulate a plan, allocate resources, then forecast from the projected impact of goals.

source_qualifier.effect: The language concerns intended assistance and projection, not a demonstrated allocation benefit.

groups.consequence: The reader knows what choices the output should inform before seeing its construction.

next_link.basis: Following text moves from promised use to operating assumptions; this relationship is inferred from textual order, not an explicit causal connector.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: A named decision role makes the purpose inspectable but does not establish utility, accuracy or causal efficacy.

groups.dominant_move: Expose the operating assumptions before the method overview.

claim.content: Input properties are taken as uniform, component indicators as representative, and data as accurate and unbiased.

support.content: Three parallel bullets specify the conditions; this block supplies no empirical test establishing them.

source_qualifier.effect: The lead-in labels the statements as premises rather than observations.

groups.consequence: The following construction is presented under declared input and representation conditions.

next_link.basis: The immediately following text names dimensions and points to construction documentation.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: Preserve the assumption label; do not present the parallel list as a completed check of comparability, representation or data reliability.
groups.neutral_skeleton: Declare [comparison premise], [representation premise] and [input-quality premise] before describing [construction].

groups.dominant_move: Decompose the output and hand off construction detail to the method section.

claim.content: The assessment has six named dimensions, each using component inputs; detailed construction is deferred to Methodology.

support.content: The dimension list and the explanation of component data make the proposed architecture visible, while the final sentence points to its detailed documentation.

source_qualifier.effect: The block describes architecture and a documentation location; it does not report a calibration or validation result.

groups.consequence: The reader can retain the dimensions while deferring technical detail, rather than encountering an unexplained index label.

next_link.basis: The next block describes the selected data and advertised capabilities alongside concrete limits.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: A component list and documentation pointer do not themselves prove validity or justify inventing a single aggregate scalar.
groups.neutral_skeleton: Name [output dimensions] -> describe [component inputs] -> point to [construction documentation].

groups.dominant_move: Put advertised data advantages beside input and agency limits.

claim.content: The authors advertise completeness, stability under small changes and manipulation resistance, while disclosing externally imposed penalties and no fallback for missing data.

support.content: Completeness is given as the reason for dataset choice. This Summary block does not report a perturbation or manipulation experiment.
The final two sentences identify a cross-boundary influence and the absence of an alternate calculation for a missing-data case.

source_qualifier.effect: These phrases delimit the assertions or reveal an uncovered case; they do not certify robustness or the rarity of missing data.

groups.consequence: An advertised advantage and its scope can be read together before the demonstration case is introduced.

next_link.basis: The source then names the selected demonstration and reports its prospective outlook.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: Do not transfer the manipulation-resistance assurance as a positive reusable result. The later accuracy and perturbation conditions must remain visible through unit031; unit034 preserves the agency boundary.
groups.neutral_skeleton: State [data-choice rationale] and [advertised capability], then disclose [external constraint] and [uncovered input case].

groups.dominant_move: Close the Summary with a selected case and a conditional future implication.

claim.content: A selected case is paired with a development plan and a twenty-year projection, followed by the possibility of serving as an exemplar.

support.content: The authors cite economic growth and relative index performance as reasons for case selection.
The text says a plan was created, future parameters were projected, and the case was predicted to maintain or increase sustainability.

source_qualifier.effect: The outlook and exemplar implication are prospective, not observed programme effects or a validated cross-country transfer.

groups.consequence: The Summary ends with a concrete intended use and a forecast, rather than ending after the list of dimensions.

next_link.basis: The next physical page opens Introduction and returns to the development-planning motivation; this is a section transition, not a continuation of the projected result.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: The embedded graphic and its caption are excluded. The text's ambitious exemplar implication is not endorsed or independently verified.
groups.neutral_skeleton: Give [case-selection rationale] -> describe [proposed programme and future setting] -> report [projection] -> qualify [possible wider implication].

groups.dominant_move: Turn competing needs and limited resources into a prioritisation task.

claim.content: Planning must consider present and future needs under uncertainty and limited resources, creating a need for explicit prioritisation.

support.content: The prose names competing generations, uncertain future factors and limited resources, then explicitly connects scarcity to the need for a method.

source_qualifier.effect: The opening describes a constrained, uncertain planning task, not a uniquely optimal ranking already established.

groups.consequence: A reader knows why prioritisation is needed before the paper introduces its operational meaning of sustainability.

next_link.basis: The next printed heading asks what sustainability looks like; the following block defines the concept and describes the development trade-off.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: Scarcity motivates an allocation method but does not validate a particular ranking or prove that the chosen representation balances competing needs.
groups.neutral_skeleton: Present [competing needs] and [uncertainty] -> disclose [resource constraint] -> motivate [prioritisation task].

groups.dominant_move: Operationalise the central concept, introduce a trade-off, then route the construct into dimensions.

claim.content: The authors interpret sustainability through persistence and stability, describe development as potentially sacrificing it, and identify six stability dimensions.

support.content: A short equivalence is expanded into an ability to maintain a process, then into a national-scale capacity.
The benefit/cost contrast motivates balance, after which the source lists the dimensions considered central to human welfare.

source_qualifier.effect: The development trade-off is presented as possible and frequent, not logically unavoidable in every case. The opening definitional equivalence itself is not qualified as one of several definitions.

groups.consequence: The conceptual discussion produces the categories needed by the following objective, rather than remaining an abstract motivation paragraph.

next_link.basis: The Objective heading takes up the forms of stability as the context for the proposed index.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: Treat the equivalence as this paper's operational choice, not the sole correct definition. The bullet list is part of the textual move, not six additional validated models or six independent language patterns.
groups.neutral_skeleton: Define [concept] through [capacity] -> restate it at [application scale] -> show [benefit/cost tension] -> name [dimensions to represent].

groups.dominant_move: Close the Introduction by connecting the proposed representation to audience actions and analytical consequences.

claim.content: The proposed index is intended to identify cases and sectors, set goals, prioritise needs, allocate resources and relate policy measures to anticipated consequences.

support.content: The paragraph lists the decisions the output should support and ends with Thus, tying policy measures and unmet needs to their effects on a measure.

source_qualifier.effect: These are proposed analytical functions. The block does not report observed policy benefits or a tested response function.

groups.consequence: The following construction has a stated purpose: supply the representation needed by the previously named decision operations.

next_link.basis: S03 is Methodology in the bound v5 source-heading map. This is a source-heading-map handoff, not new inspection of equations or confirmation of the causal capability promised in the Introduction.

groups.editorial_reuse_boundary: Analytical consequence must not silently become measured treatment effect. This is the Introduction-closing variant of the Summary purpose mechanism, not a second independent support entity.
groups.neutral_skeleton: Name [representation] -> enumerate [audience operations] -> connect [need and action] to [analytical consequence] -> hand off to [construction].

positive_route.opening_skeleton_review: The placeholder versions retain a purpose-to-premise-to-construction-to-scope-to-demonstration Summary route and a constraint-to-meaning-to-objective Introduction route. This is an editorial opening-only readability check, not a full-paper organization skeleton pass.
positive_route.full_paper_skeleton_status: not-accepted: official task coverage, full model/result paths and visually reconciled paragraph chains remain unverified

exclusions: Page1 embedded graphic; line46 after column8 is its caption and is excluded
Page2 running header and non-prose blank lines; printed headings locate transitions but are not counted as body sentences
All formula/symbol work, charts, tables and references outside these opening prose ranges
support_count_policy: No new units, patterns, examples, observations, rules or independent source papers. Existing v13 candidate counts remain41/40/82; this adds resolvable argument roles, not new evidence multiplicity.
